etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English countable, equivalent to count (“to enumerate”) +‎ -able.

definitions.definition: Capable of being counted; having a quantity.
(mathematics, of a set) finite or countably infinite; having a one-to-one correspondence (bijection) with a subset of the natural numbers.
(mathematics, of a set) Countably infinite; having a bijection with the natural numbers.
(grammar, of a noun) Freely usable with the indefinite article and with numbers.

quote.citation: 2014, James Lambert, “Diachronic stability in Indian English lexis”, in World Englishes, page 112:
quote.text: In these extracts the word abuse is used in the sense of ‘an individual piece of invective’ or ‘an abusive comment’ and is clearly a countable noun.
